title: The Annual Policy Fee Falling Due With a Settlement of a Supplement Premium Account
content:
The policy fee on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is charged once a policy year and falls due with a settlement of the premium account. What is added for it is settled from the entries standing on that account.

1. Where no entry carrying the policy fee stands on the account for the 12 months to date and the settlement covers a span of 12 months, the whole annual policy fee is added.
2. Where an entry carrying the policy fee stands on the account for the 12 months to date, nothing further is added for the policy fee.
3. Where neither of those holds, the share of the annual policy fee falling on the months the billing period now current covers is added.

### Reading the three cases

The first case requires both of its limbs: no entry carrying the policy fee on the account for the 12 months to date, and a settlement covering a span of 12 months. Where the fee has not been charged in those 12 months but the settlement covers a shorter span, the first case is not reached and the third governs.

The second case turns on a single question, whether an entry carrying the policy fee stands on the account for the 12 months to date. Where one does, nothing further is added whatever the span covers.

The third case takes the annual fee spread over the twelve months of the policy year and adds the share falling on the months the billing period now current covers.

### Hypothetical figures

On Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan K, with no entry carrying the policy fee on the account for the 12 months to date and a settlement covering a span of 12 months: the whole annual policy fee of 24.00 is added.

On the same plan letter, with an entry carrying the policy fee standing on the account within the 12 months to date: nothing further is added for the policy fee.

On Ridgecrest Medicare Supplement Plan D, with no entry carrying the policy fee on the account for the 12 months to date and a billing period now current covering 3 months: the annual policy fee of 20.00 spread over the twelve months of the policy year gives a monthly share, and the share falling on those 3 months, rounded to the cent, is 5.00.
